maml:description.maml:para: Lists the CSS property names the scanner reports, with where each one was announced

Returns the contents of Data/RetiredProperties.psd1 as objects: the 58 retired names Microsoft lists on the CSS template reference page, counting the longhands it folds into the position and margin bullets, and the short Review list of near misses the scanner flags for a person to read.
FirstListedIn says where a retired name was first announced, which is the point of the command. Message Center post MC1435782 (July 2026) carried 19 names; MC1458474 (August 2026) added 28; 11 more, including display and visibility, appear only on the Learn page. A tenant checked against the first post alone can have a false all-clear.
[String[]] (Optional)
Retired, Review, or both. Defaults to both.
This command takes no pipeline input.

One per name: Property, Level (Retired or Review), Bullet (the Learn bullet the name came from, Retired only), FirstListedIn (MC1435782, MC1458474 or Learn; Retired only), Reason (Review only), SourceUrl and SourceDate.

maml:introduction.maml:para: Confirms the list a scan is using: 49 bullets on the Learn page, plus the 5 and 4 longhands it folds under position and margin.

command:example.maml:title: --------- Example 2: How many names each announcement introduced ---------

maml:introduction.maml:para: ```powershell Get-EntraBrandingCssProperty -Level Retired | Group-Object FirstListedIn | Select-Object Name, Count ```
Shows why a check against the first Message Center post alone misses 39 names. Review entries have no FirstListedIn, which is why -Level Retired is passed here.

command:example.maml:title: --------- Example 3: The near misses and why each is listed ---------

maml:introduction.maml:para: ```Output Property : -webkit-filter Reason : Vendor form of filter, which is retired. Microsoft lists only the unprefixed name.
Property : all Reason : Shorthand that resets every property, including display and visibility, which are retired. ```
The Review list is deliberately short and never reported as Retired. Reading the reason is how to decide whether a Review finding needs action.

maml:description.maml:para: Finds retired CSS properties in Entra ID company branding, from files or a tenant

Microsoft Entra ID is retiring the layout and positioning properties in company branding custom CSS. From October 26, 2026 they are blocked and stop working, with no supported replacement. This command parses custom CSS into declarations and reports every one that uses a retired property, so an admin can see what will break before it does.
Two sources feed the same scanner:
File mode (-Path) reads one or more .css files, which is where a download from the Entra admin center lands, and takes pipeline input from Get-ChildItem.
Tenant mode (-Tenant) reads every company branding localization in the connected tenant through Microsoft Graph, and with -IncludeTheme every branding theme localization as well. It needs Microsoft.Graph.Authentication and an existing Connect-MgGraph session; the full Graph SDK is not required. Every call is a GET. The command never writes to the tenant.
One result comes out per source, with a Status that keeps "no custom CSS present" (NoCustomCss) separate from "custom CSS present and nothing found" (Clean), because those are different statements. Retired means at least one declaration uses a retired property; Review means none did but a near miss is worth reading; Error means a tenant source could not be read. The Findings property holds one object per flagged declaration with its selector, at-rule context, line and column.
Matching is on the property name after comments are stripped, strings and url(...) are skipped, and CSS escapes are decoded. A value is never matched, so transform: scale(1.2) reports transform and not scale, and custom properties such as --display are ignored. The retired list lives in Data/RetiredProperties.psd1 beside its source URL; Get-EntraBrandingCssProperty shows it.
[Switch] (Optional, tenant mode)
Also read branding theme localizations. Themes exist only in the Graph beta API, so this is opt-in.
[String] (Optional, tenant mode)
The tenant id, as a GUID. Discovered from GET /organization when omitted, which is the usual case. Required when that call returns more than one organization.
[String[]] (Mandatory in file mode, Pipeline: ByValue, ByPropertyName as FullName)
One or more .css files. Wildcards are allowed. Each file becomes one result; a file that cannot be read, or a path that does not exist, is reported with Write-Error and the rest continue.
[ScriptBlock] (Optional, tenant mode)
[Switch] (Mandatory in tenant mode)

Read the connected tenant's branding over Microsoft Graph instead of files. Requires a Connect-MgGraph session with a scope that can read organizational branding; OrganizationalBranding.Read.All is the least privileged one Microsoft documents for every call this makes.
File paths, with wildcards allowed. Objects with a FullName property, such as the output of Get-ChildItem, bind by property name.

One per source scanned. Source, SourceType (File, Localization or Theme), Name, Status (NoCustomCss, Clean, Review, Retired or Error), HasCustomCss, RetiredCount, ReviewCount, DeclarationCount, Length, CustomCssRelativeUrl (tenant mode), Findings and Error. Each entry in Findings is an EntraBrandingCss.Finding with Source, Level, Property, Value, Important, Selector, AtRule, Line, Column, FirstListedIn and Note.

TROUBLESHOOTING: - See the README in the module folder.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ```Output Name SourceType Status Retired Review Declarations ---- ---------- ------ ------- ------ ------------ custom-styles.css File Retired 2 0 15 ```

Scans the CSS file downloaded from the Entra admin center (Company branding, Edit, Layout, Custom CSS, Download). One result comes back with the status, the counts, and a Findings property holding each flagged declaration. Use this to check a branding file before the October 26, 2026 retirement.

command:example.maml:title: --------- Example 2: Every retired declaration across a folder ---------

maml:introduction.maml:para: ```powershell Get-ChildItem .\branding\*.css | Test-EntraBrandingCss | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Findings | Where-Object Level -eq 'Retired' | Format-Table Source, Property, Value, Selector, Line ```

Get-ChildItem output binds to -Path through its FullName property, so a folder of branding files kept for several tenants is scanned in one pipeline. Expanding Findings gives one row per retired declaration with the file it came from.

```Output Name SourceType Status Retired Review Declarations ---- ---------- ------ ------- ------ ------------ 0 Localization NoCustomCss 0 0 0 fr-FR Localization Retired 1 0 4 Contoso (en-US) Theme Clean 0 0 9 ```

Reads every company branding localization, and with -IncludeTheme every branding theme localization, through Microsoft Graph. A locale with no custom CSS is reported as NoCustomCss so it is not mistaken for a locale that was checked and found clean. Every request is a GET.
